books.section: Topic 1.3 European exploration in the Americas
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

parts.modelAnswer: One term moved the dividing line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands, giving Portugal the lands east of the line, including Brazil. Spain received the lands west of the line, which was most of the Americas.
parts.prompt: Identify one term of the Treaty of Tordesillas.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for naming one accurate term of the treaty, such as the 370-league line, Portugal receiving Brazil, or Spain receiving the lands west of the line.
scoring.notEarned: Naming only that Spain and Portugal divided lands, with no term, does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: Both crowns were Catholic and recognized the pope as an authority who could settle disputes between Catholic rulers. Accepting his mediation gave the division a legitimacy neither crown could claim on its own.
parts.prompt: Explain why Spain and Portugal accepted the pope's role in dividing the lands.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining why the crowns accepted papal mediation, such as shared Catholic faith or the pope's recognized authority.
scoring.notEarned: Stating only that the pope divided the lands, with no reason the crowns accepted it, does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: The treaty secured Portugal's claim to Brazil, which became the one Portuguese colony in the Americas. It also protected Portugal's African sea route to Asia, since the line kept Spain out of the eastern seas.
parts.prompt: Explain one consequence of the treaty for Portugal.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one accurate consequence for Portugal, such as Brazil, the African sea route, or the protection of its eastern trade.
scoring.notEarned: Stating only that Portugal got land, with no consequence explained, does not earn the point.

stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question, summarizing the Treaty of Tordesillas (1494).
stimulus.text: Original secondary passage written for this question. In 1493, the pope drew a line through the Atlantic giving Spain the lands west of it and Portugal the lands east. Portugal objected, since the line left it little room in the Atlantic, and in 1494 Spain and Portugal signed the Treaty of Tordesillas, moving the line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands. The new line gave Portugal Brazil and kept Spain's claim to the rest of the Americas.
